transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, um, what brought me in is I just can’t seem to keep things in order at work anymore. I’m in laundry and dry cleaning, and it’s like the tickets, receipts, little workshop notes, customer jobs—everything ends up in piles together, and then I’m standing there not knowing what to handle first.

It sounds silly, but it gets away from me. Like, one customer’s order slip will be mixed in with receipts from yesterday, and then I’ll remember I was supposed to check something, but I can’t find the note. Then I start sorting one pile and somehow make three more piles. My daughter says I need better folders, which maybe I do, but I’ve bought folders before and then they just become another place I lose things. So… that’s why I’m here.
Can you tell me if you have similar problems with staying organized or keeping track of things at home or in other parts of your life, like managing personal tasks or responsibilities?

At home… yeah, I mean, it’s kind of the same sort of thing, but work is where it really shows because there’s so many little papers. Tickets, receipts, those notes from the back room, customer jobs waiting—everything ends up in one pile, and then I’m looking at it like, “Okay, what was I supposed to do first?”

At home it’s more like… well, I’ll put something down meaning to deal with it, and then I’ve covered it with something else. My kitchen table gets like my counter at work. But the work stuff is what scares me more because it affects other people’s orders. I’ll start trying to sort it, then I find a receipt from yesterday, then I think about a different customer, and suddenly I’m not doing the thing I started doing.
Do you find yourself getting distracted or losing track of what you're doing in other areas of your life, like when you're talking with friends, reading something, or working on a hobby?

Yeah, I do. Like if I’m going over the day’s dry-cleaning orders, I can start off fine, you know, checking the slips and what needs to be done. But after a few minutes my head is somewhere else—like I’ll notice a label on something, and then I’m thinking about choir plans, or something I need to handle at home.

And then I kind of snap back and realize I missed half of what I was supposed to be checking. It’s frustrating because I was looking right at it, but I wasn’t really taking it in.
Do you find it hard to stay focused during conversations with others, like when someone is talking to you and your mind wanders or you lose track of what they’re saying?

Yeah… yes, that happens. Like my helper will be standing right in front of me, telling me, “This customer wants starch,” or “No starch on these shirts,” and I’m nodding like I’m listening.

And then, I don’t know, I’ll notice the tag or think about where that order needs to go, or—well, sometimes she talks fast too, but still—a minute later I have to ask her, “Wait, what did you just say?” It’s embarrassing because she just told me, and I was right there.
Do you often find yourself forgetting things or losing items that you need to get your work or daily tasks done, like keys, paperwork, or tools?

Oh yes, all the time. I’m always hunting for something I just had—like the tagging gun, or my glasses, or a customer’s ticket. Sometimes it’s that little notebook I carry around, and I’ll swear I just put it down by the counter, but then it’s under a stack of slips or over by the press.

And then everybody’s waiting while I’m looking for it, and I feel bad because it slows the whole place down. It’s not like I mean to be careless, it’s just… things disappear on me.

No strong evidence supporting recurrent depressive episodes (F33.0) or unspecified neurotic disorder (F48.8)) has been identified.
